diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any bounded function $v : [0,1] \times \mathbb{R}^{3d} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the time and spatial H\"older-Lipschitz condition:
It is clear that $v^{\varepsilon} \in C_{b}^{\infty}$, and the standard mollification estimates, together with the regularity of $v$, imply:

issues.failure_explanation: The construction averages v(t−τ,·) over τ∈[−ε²,0], i.e. over times in [t,t+ε²], yet it is declared for functions defined only on [0,1]×R^{3d}. Hence v^ε is undefined for t∈(1−ε²,1]. The smoothed functions and their supersolution/scheme properties are nevertheless asserted on all of [h,1]×R^{3d}, and the comparison conclusion is claimed on [0,1]×R^{3d}, i.e. exactly at the terminal time t=1 where Theorem main theorem CLT is evaluated.

failure_location.quote: v^{\varepsilon}(t,x,y,z) := (v \ast \zeta_{\varepsilon})(t,x,y,z) := \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e) \, de \, d\tau,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend u and u_h slightly beyond t=1 (u_h by its own recursion, u by the Feynman–Kac formula for the nonlinear Lévy process at times >1), or use a one-sided mollifier and re-run the comparison on the corresponding time window; all stated bounds then hold on [0,1].
issues.overall_effect: The regularization step of the proof of Theorem main theorem is not well posed on a neighbourhood of t=1, so the error bounds (and therefore the rates obtained from them) are unproved at and near t=1.
issues.title: Mollification v^ε is not well defined near the terminal time t = 1
issues.why_classification: The gap is confined to a boundary layer in one technical construction; a local extension of the time domain (or a one-sided mollifier) restores every estimate, guarantee and rate without new arguments.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated justification, Lemma uh_regularity (ii), only gives |u_h(t)−u_h(s)| ≤ C(|t−s|^{1/2}+h^{1/2}); smoothing over a time window of width ε² therefore yields ‖u_h−u_h^ε‖_∞ = O(ε+h^{1/2}), not O(ε). This loss is real: u_h is piecewise constant in t on the grid {kh} with jumps of order h^{1/2} (e.g. for φ(x)=min(|x|,1) with a non-degenerate Gaussian X₁), so for ε ≪ h^{1/2} the mollification error is of order h^{1/2} and the claimed bound fails. The adjacent derivative bound correctly retains the factor (ε+h^{1/2}), exposing the inconsistency.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by ‖u_h−u_h^ε‖_∞ ≤ C(ε+h^{1/2}) in the mollification estimate and in the initial comparison (or restrict the ε-minimisation to ε ≥ h^{1/2}); the extra h^{1/2} contribution is absorbed by the existing h^{1/2} terms and by the final rate.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit bounds of Theorem main theorem (with the term 4C₀ε) and their restatement in Theorem main theorem CLT are not established as written; at best an additional O(h^{1/2}) term, or a restriction ε ≳ h^{1/2}, is needed. The rates Γ(α,δ,q₀) are unaffected because h^{1/2} is dominated by h^Γ.
issues.title: Mollification error bound ‖u_h−u_h^ε‖≤2C₀ε ignores the h^{1/2} time jumps of u_h
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of one error term (or a restriction on ε) preserves every statement and every rate; only the modulus of continuity already proved in Lemma uh_regularity is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using H\"older's inequality with $p_1 = 3$, $q_1 = \frac{3}{2}$, and $p_2 = q_2 = 2$, it follows that
The range of $\delta$ arises from technical constraints when applying H\"{o}lder's inequality to estimate $R_{21}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The key bound interpolates |Δ_xω| ≤ min(2‖D_xω‖, ‖D²_{xz}ω‖ h^{1/α}|Z|) as |Δ_xω|^{q₁} ≤ (2‖D_xω‖)^{q₁−δ}(‖D²_{xz}ω‖h^{1/α}|Z|)^δ. This requires δ ≤ q₁ = 3/2; for δ > q₁ the exponent q₁−δ is negative and the inequality reverses. It is genuinely false: taking ω with D_xω varying slowly in z (‖D²_{xz}ω‖ = ‖D_xω‖/(κh^{1/α}) with κ→∞) makes |Δ_xω| ≈ ‖D_xω||Z|/κ while the claimed right-hand side decays like κ^{−δ}, so the estimate — and with it the term h^{(4δ−3α)/(6α)}‖D_xω‖^{(3−2δ)/3}‖D²_{xz}ω‖^{2δ/3} of Lemma consistency, whose exponent (3−2δ)/3 is negative for δ>3/2 — fails by an unbounded factor. Assumption (v) allows δ ∈ ((3/4)α ∨ 1, α), which contains values above 3/2 whenever α > 3/2, and Remark remark_delta derives only the lower bound δ > αq₁/2 and never imposes δ ≤ q₁.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Cap the moment exponent at 3/2 (use δ ∧ 3/2 throughout, which loses no distributions since an upper δ-moment implies a 3/2-moment) and state the rates as Γ(α, δ∧3/2, q₀); equivalently run the Hölder step with q₁ = max(3/2,δ) and weaken the rate accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: For α ∈ (3/2,2) and δ ∈ (3/2,α) the consistency bound of Lemma consistency is false, so the explicit errors E₁,E₂ of Theorem main theorem, the two-sided Berry–Esseen bound of Theorem main theorem CLT and the rates Γ(α,δ,q₀) of Theorems main theorem ex1 CLT and main theorem ex1 (including the advertised supremum rate 1/(4α+6)) are not established. For α ≤ 3/2 nothing is affected.
issues.title: Consistency estimate uses an interpolation requiring δ ≤ q₁ = 3/2, which Assumption (v) does not ensure
issues.why_classification: Capping δ at 3/2 needs no new architecture and keeps both error bounds and a power-law rate, so the result stays recognisably the same; but the advertised exponent is materially smaller in the regime α ∈ (3/2,2) (at most (2−α)/(4α) instead of up to 1/(4α+6)) — a limited weakening rather than a major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof produces the term ½‖∂²_tω‖_∞ h, which carries no moment factor, but the statement absorbs every term into 2M₀{…} where M₀ is a sum of moments of (X₁,Y₁,Z₁). Such an absorption needs M₀ ≥ 1/4, and the assumptions allow all these moments to be arbitrarily small (e.g. X₁=Y₁=0 and Z₁ of arbitrarily small α-stable activity, which is compatible with (iii) and (vi) for the matching Θ). Concretely, for ω(t,x,y,z)=ψ(t) one has G=0 and l̂=0, so R = |ψ′(t)−(ψ(t)−ψ(t−h))/h| = ½h|ψ″(t)|+o(h), whereas the stated right-hand side is 2M₀h‖ψ″‖_∞, which is smaller whenever M₀ < 1/4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Enlarge the constant, e.g. replace M₀ by M₀ ∨ ½ (or 2M₀ by 2M₀+1) in Lemma consistency and in the definitions of E₁ and E₂.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma consistency is false in admissible low-activity regimes, and through the definitions of E₁,E₂ the explicit error bounds of Theorems main theorem and main theorem CLT inherit the wrong constant; convergence rates are unchanged once the constant is enlarged.
issues.title: Constant 2M₀ in the consistency bound cannot dominate the pure time-discretisation error
issues.why_classification: Only a constant in a technical estimate is wrong; enlarging it is a purely local one-line correction that leaves every claim, regime and rate intact.
